chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma'il ibn Mihran from al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Bata'ini from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Whoever passes three days without reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in them, he is forsaken, and the noose of faith is removed from his neck; and if he dies during these three days, he will be a disbeliever in Allah, the Great.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on not reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas for three days?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-Amal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) emphasis on the consistent recitation of Surah al-Ikhlas as a vital spiritual practice for sustaining faith. The hadith establishes a specific timeframe of three days; missing this period is described as removing the 'rope of faith' from one's neck, leading to a state of disbelief if death occurs within that window. This highlights the Shia scholarly view of Surah al-Ikhlas not merely as a chapter of the Quran, but as a fundamental pillar of daily devotional life and theological affirmation.
